title: Mastering Scroll State in UI Design
summary: This lesson explains why scroll position should be treated as application state, particularly in single-page applications. It covers scroll restoration, offsetting for sticky headers, and the usability issues of infinite scroll with footers.

transcript.text: You hit back and lost the exact post you scrolled down to.
Your single page app resets scroll to zero on every route change.
The browser used to remember for you. Your router forgot how.
Save the scroll position for each history entry, then put it back when the user returns, instead of dumping them at the very top.
A sticky header hides the row you land on. Offset the restore by its height. Otherwise, you land close but wrong.
Jump links need scroll-margin-top, or every heading tucks up under the bar. The anchor lands and the title is invisible.
Infinite scroll pushes the footer one step further, forever. Your links, your contact, your terms all live down there. Nobody ever reaches them.
Scroll is state. Go to designmotionhq.com for more. Link in bio.

design_principles: Header height offsets for scroll-to-element actions
Avoid infinite scroll if the footer contains essential navigation
before_after: Demonstrates the difference between a broken scroll experience (resetting to top or hiding content under headers) versus a corrected experience using manual restoration and offsets.
